course: Cisco ACI Upgrade Automation with Claude
source_input: Client use case 10, 'Cisco ACI Upgrade Automation: Managing upgrade of ACI chassis as per process suggested by Cisco', with the client's aim 'to do automation using Claude for all these content' and course names of the form 'Automation of <> using Claude'. Use case 2 (device upgrades with space clear, firmware upload, pre and post checks and a scheduler option) shaped the bootflash, staging and scheduling modules.
why_this_course: ACI upgrades follow a documented Cisco sequence: back up, download images, validate, update CIMC, upgrade the APIC cluster, validate again, wait for Fully Fit, then upgrade switch groups [c2]. Most of the risk sits in the details: groups that put both vPC peers down at once, an unhealthy cluster, bootflash without room for the image, or an operator reloading an APIC when an upgrade stalls [c3][c12][c15]. These are exactly the steps where checklists get skipped under weekend pressure.

The work is also well suited to automation with a clear split. Reading validator output, joining it with inventory and writing a plan and a report is language-heavy work that Claude does well, while creating policies and triggering groups must be deterministic, approved and logged. Cisco exposes every step through the APIC REST API and Ansible modules [c7][c10][c22], and Claude's Agent SDK can return plans as schema-validated JSON [c26], so the course can teach a workflow where the model never touches a write path.

The client asked for automation of ACI upgrades 'as per process suggested by Cisco'. The course therefore follows Cisco's guide chapter by chapter [c1] and adds the controls an enterprise change board expects: a pull request, a ServiceNow change, window enforcement and an audit log.

design_decisions.decision: Follow Cisco's documented workflow as the spine of the course.
design_decisions.rationale: The client input says 'as per process suggested by Cisco'; mapping modules to the guide's workflow keeps the course defensible and current [c1][c2].

design_decisions.decision: Claude plans and explains; Python and Ansible execute.
design_decisions.rationale: Write actions on a fabric must be repeatable and reviewable; the agent has read-only MCP tools and denied write tools, enforced by permissions and hooks, not prompts [c24][c27][c28].

design_decisions.decision: Use structured outputs and a code gate for the plan.
design_decisions.rationale: A plan that breaks a grouping rule must be rejected before a person reads it; the SDK's JSON Schema output plus Python rule checks make that testable [c3][c26].

design_decisions.decision: Put approval in both GitHub and ServiceNow.
design_decisions.rationale: Engineers review the plan as code in a PR with required checks, and the change board approves the window in ServiceNow; the runner checks both [c32][c36].

design_decisions.decision: Bring in the bootflash, staging and scheduler items from use case 2.
design_decisions.rationale: Space clearing, firmware upload, pre and post checks and scheduling were explicit client asks; on ACI they map to the bootflash check, the firmware repository and window enforcement [c12][c17][c21].

design_decisions.decision: Use a small physical fabric plus a mocked APIC.
design_decisions.rationale: Real reboots and cluster conversion cannot be shown on the DevNet simulator, and failure paths cannot be safely forced on hardware, so both are used [c37].

modules.title: The Cisco ACI upgrade process and where upgrades go wrong
modules.goal: Learners can describe Cisco's recommended ACI upgrade sequence end to end and map every step to the APIC objects and checks it touches.
learning_objectives: Learners can list Cisco's upgrade workflow in order, from backup and image download through APIC cluster, switch groups and post-checks [c2].
Learners can explain the group design rules that keep one vPC peer, one APIC-connected leaf and one route-reflector spine up during every group [c3].
Learners can name the APIC objects that represent the firmware repository, controller and switch firmware targets, maintenance policies and groups [c7][c10].
Learners can state the course pattern: Claude plans and explains, deterministic code executes, a person approves, everything is logged.

lessons.title: Cisco's documented sequence
points: Walk the guide structure so learners know where each answer lives: overview, architecture, checklists, mixed-version operations, and GUI, REST and CLI procedures [c1].

The workflow order: AES-encrypted config export, disable App Center apps, download APIC and switch images to the APICs, pre-upgrade validation, CIMC/HUU update, APIC upgrade, validate again, wait for Fully Fit, then switches [c2].
A multistep upgrade repeats the whole cycle from the intermediate release; plan two windows, not one [c2].
Target release selection: use the Upgrade/Downgrade Support Matrix with from and to releases to see behavior changes and open bugs on the path [c19].
Read release notes for every release between current and target (Changes in Behavior) plus Open and Known Issues for the target, for both APIC and switches [c12].
CIMC is part of the plan: release notes say to install only the CIMC versions in the compatibility table, and point to advisories such as CSCwo74485 for specific APIC servers [c9].

lessons.title: Where ACI upgrades go wrong
points: Both vPC peers in one group: Cisco wants one leaf of each vPC pair running, and from 4.2(5) concurrency in a group is unlimited by default, so a careless group reboots both peers together [c3].
Unpaired leaves: the checklist warns that without vPC pairs the built-in protection against simultaneous leaf upgrades does not work [c12].
An APIC cluster that is not Fully Fit, uncleared faults, NTP drift between nodes and bootflash usage above the F1820/F1821 thresholds are all called out as blockers [c12].
Bootflash matters because the switch checks filesystem and bootflash space before extracting the image, and auto-cleanup above 50% can even delete the boot image [c14][c12].
During a stalled upgrade the wrong reflex causes the damage: do not reload an APIC, do not decommission one, and do not flip the firmware target back [c15].
TAC experience: never reboot two or more APICs at the same time, and do nothing on APIC2 or APIC3 while APIC1 is still upgrading [c20].

lessons.title: The APIC object model for upgrades
points: Image repository: firmwareRepoP with a firmwareOSource child posted to /api/node/mo/uni/fabric.xml [c7].
Controller target and trigger: firmwareCtrlrFwP (version, ignoreCompat) and maintCtrlrMaintP (adminState up, adminSt triggered) under uni/controller [c7].
Switch policy and group from 4.0(1): maintMaintP carries version and runMode, maintMaintGrp holds fabricNodeBlk ranges and a maintRsMgrpp relation to the policy [c10].
Status classes for checking progress: firmwareCtrlrRunning, firmwareRunning and maintUpgJob [c11].

Scheduler note: from 5.1 the GUI no longer offers a scheduler for upgrades; the Ansible maintenance policy module still requires one, so the course keeps window enforcement in its own code [c17][c22].

lessons.title: The teaching pattern for this course
points: Claude reads validator output, inventory and release notes, proposes plans and drafts reports; it never holds credentials that can write to the fabric.
Python and Ansible create policies and trigger groups only after a GitHub pull request and a ServiceNow change are approved.
Every prompt, tool call, APIC API call and approval lands in one audit log that the change board can read.
The MCP specification itself says a human should be able to deny tool invocations and that tool use should be logged, which is the same rule applied to the fabric [c29].

instructor_demo: Open the Cisco upgrade guide and show the chapter list, then the workflow page, reading the order aloud [c1][c2].
Run the Support Matrix for the lab's current release to the course target release and show the behavior changes and open bugs it returns [c19].
In the lab APIC GUI, open Admin > Firmware and show controllers, switches and images, then open the API Inspector and capture the calls the page makes.
Query /api/node/class/firmwareRunning.json and /api/node/class/maintUpgJob.json in a browser tab and relate the JSON to the GUI [c11].
Draw the lab fabric (3 APICs, 4 leaves in two vPC pairs, 2 spines) and ask the room which two switches must never share a group [c3].
Show the guidelines page section on what not to do when an upgrade stalls and put it on the wall as the course's stop rules [c15].

lab.brief: Walk the lab fabric in the APIC GUI and API Inspector, map each Cisco process step to the APIC objects it touches, and write the workflow brief.
steps: Log in to the lab APIC GUI and record the current APIC and switch versions from Admin > Firmware.
Open the API Inspector, refresh the Firmware pages and copy the class queries it shows into notes.md.
Run the same queries with curl after an aaaLogin and save the raw JSON under fixtures/ [c8].
Fill the process table: for each Cisco workflow step, list the APIC object or class it reads or writes [c2][c7][c10].
Mark the lab's vPC pairs, APIC-connected leaves and route-reflector spines on the topology sheet [c3].
List the blockers the checklist names and note which ones the lab can show today (faults, NTP, bootflash, cluster health) [c12].
Write the one-page ACI upgrade workflow brief: sequence, objects, stop rules and who approves what.
Peer-review another team's brief against the Cisco workflow page.
success_criteria: The brief lists every Cisco workflow step in the documented order, including validation before and after the APIC upgrade [c2].
Each step maps to at least one named APIC class or object.
The topology sheet correctly identifies both vPC pairs and the spines that must stay up per group [c3].
The stop rules include no APIC reload and no target change during a stalled upgrade [c15].

common_pitfalls: Treating the switch upgrade as one big group because concurrency is unlimited from 4.2(5) [c3].
Skipping the second validation run after the APIC upgrade [c2].
Choosing a target release from memory instead of the Support Matrix and release notes [c19].
Ignoring CIMC compatibility because 'it is only the server' [c9].
Confusing GUI scheduling with policy scheduling; from 5.1 the GUI has no scheduler option [c17].

knowledge_check.q: Why must the APIC cluster be Fully Fit before switch upgrades start?
knowledge_check.a: Cisco's workflow upgrades the APICs first and only moves to ACI-mode switches once all APICs are Fully Fit; a degraded cluster cannot safely orchestrate switch upgrades [c2].

knowledge_check.q: Which three things must stay up in every switch group?
knowledge_check.a: One leaf of each vPC pair, one leaf connected to each APIC, and at least one route-reflector spine and one IPN-connected spine per pod [c3].

knowledge_check.q: Which class tells you upgrade job status for both controllers and switches?
knowledge_check.a: maintUpgJob, queried at /api/node/class/maintUpgJob [c11].

knowledge_check.q: An upgrade stalls at 75% on APIC2. Name two things you must not do.
knowledge_check.a: Do not reload any APIC and do not switch the firmware target back to the original version; Cisco also says not to decommission a controller [c15][c20].

modules.title: Claude Code, Agent SDK and MCP setup for the ACI workflow
modules.goal: Learners stand up a project where Claude can query the fabric through read-only MCP tools and return schema-shaped answers, with no path to write actions.
learning_objectives: Learners can install Claude Code, create a project CLAUDE.md that encodes the upgrade rules, and confirm it loaded [c24].
Learners can build and register a stdio MCP server that exposes read-only APIC queries [c25][c30].
Learners can call the Agent SDK with an output schema and read structured_output from the result [c26].
Learners can configure permissions so the agent can observe the fabric but cannot run write commands [c28].

lessons.title: Project setup and CLAUDE.md
points: Install Claude Code with the native installer or npm and confirm with claude --version and claude doctor; a Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise or Console account is needed.
Create ./CLAUDE.md (or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md); /init can draft one and /context shows whether it loaded [c24].
Encode the course rules there: APIC cluster first, vPC peers never in one group, never trigger a maintenance policy, always cite the query behind a claim.
Keep the file under about 200 lines and import the long runbook with @docs/upgrade-rules.md [c24].
Stress that CLAUDE.md is context, not enforcement; anything that must never happen is blocked by permissions or a PreToolUse hook [c24][c27].

lessons.title: A read-only APIC MCP server
points: Install the Python SDK with pip install "mcp[cli]" (Python 3.11+) and register tools with @mcp.tool(); type hints and docstrings become the input schema [c30].

Expose only GET-backed tools: get_nodes (fabricNode), get_controller_firmware (firmwareCtrlrRunning), get_switch_firmware (firmwareRunning), get_faults (faultInst with severity filter), get_cluster_health (infraWiNode) [c8][c11].
Each tool logs in with aaaLogin, refreshes with aaaRefresh before refreshTimeoutSeconds expires, and never accepts a URL or method from the model [c8].
Return structuredContent with an outputSchema so the client can validate tool results, and set isError for API failures instead of raising [c29].
Test with uv run mcp dev server.py in the MCP Inspector before connecting Claude [c30].

lessons.title: Registering the server with Claude Code
points: claude mcp add --transport stdio --env APIC_HOST=... --scope project apic-ro -- python mcp/apic_ro.py writes .mcp.json for the team [c25].
Use ${APIC_USER} and ${APIC_PASS} expansion in .mcp.json so credentials stay in the environment, not in the repository [c25].
Project-scoped servers need approval on first use; /mcp shows status and the tool count [c25].
Server-side rate limiting and input validation are the server's job under the MCP spec, not the model's [c29].

lessons.title: Structured outputs and permissions in the Agent SDK
points: Define Inventory and UpgradePlan as Pydantic models and pass output_format={'type': 'json_schema', 'schema': Model.model_json_schema()} [c26].
Read message.structured_output only when subtype is success; handle error_max_structured_output_retries as a failed run [c26].
The SDK validates against JSON Schema draft-07; keep schemas focused and make fields optional when data may be missing [c26].
Lock the agent down: allowed_tools=['mcp__apic-ro__*', 'Read'], disallowed_tools=['Bash', 'Write', 'Edit'], permission_mode='dontAsk' for headless runs [c28].
Remember allowed_tools does not limit bypassPermissions mode, and deny rules apply in every mode [c28].

instructor_demo: Show the finished repository layout: CLAUDE.md, .mcp.json, mcp/apic_ro.py, schemas/, runner/ and audit/.
Run /init in a fresh copy, then replace the generated text with the course rules and show /context listing the file [c24].
Start the MCP server in the Inspector and call get_switch_firmware against the lab APIC [c30].
Register it with claude mcp add at project scope and show the resulting .mcp.json [c25].
Ask Claude Code 'Which leaves are vPC peers and what are they running?' and point out that every fact came from a tool call.
Ask Claude to 'trigger the upgrade for leaf-101' and show that no tool exists and Bash is denied [c28].

lab.brief: Stand up the MCP server against the lab APIC and have Claude Code answer fabric questions using only the exposed tools.
steps: Clone the starter repository and install Claude Code; run claude doctor.
Write CLAUDE.md with the upgrade rules and import docs/upgrade-rules.md [c24].
Implement the five read-only tools in mcp/apic_ro.py with aaaLogin and aaaRefresh handling [c8][c30].
Add an outputSchema to each tool and return structuredContent [c29].
Test every tool in the MCP Inspector against the lab APIC or the DevNet simulator [c30][c37].
Register the server at project scope with environment-variable credentials [c25].
Add .claude/settings.json deny rules for Bash, Write and Edit outside the repo, and a hook that blocks any tool name containing 'trigger' [c27].
Ask Claude Code five fabric questions and save the transcript to evidence/module2.md.
success_criteria: All five tools return schema-valid JSON from the lab APIC.
No credential appears in the repository or the transcript.
Claude Code answers each question with tool calls only and names the class it queried.
An attempt to run a shell command or write a policy is refused by settings or hook [c27][c28].

common_pitfalls: Letting a tool accept an arbitrary APIC URL, which turns a read-only server into a generic API proxy.
Forgetting aaaRefresh so long sessions fail mid-demo after the session timeout [c8].
Putting the password in .mcp.json instead of using ${VAR} expansion [c25].
Relying on CLAUDE.md wording to stop write actions instead of permissions and hooks [c24].
Declaring a draft 2020-12 schema; the SDK validates with draft-07 [c26].

knowledge_check.q: Where should the rule 'never trigger a maintenance policy' be enforced?
knowledge_check.a: In permissions and hooks (and by not exposing any write tool); CLAUDE.md is context that Claude follows, not an enforced control [c24][c27].

knowledge_check.q: What does an MCP tool return when the APIC call fails?
knowledge_check.a: A tool result with isError: true and a text explanation, rather than a protocol error [c29].

knowledge_check.q: Where does the validated plan appear in an Agent SDK run?
knowledge_check.a: In structured_output on the ResultMessage when subtype is success [c26].

knowledge_check.q: Why is permission_mode 'dontAsk' useful for a CI run?
knowledge_check.a: Any call that would prompt is denied, so only pre-approved tools run; there is no human to answer prompts in CI [c28].

modules.title: Fabric discovery through the APIC REST API
modules.goal: Learners build and test a Python discovery client that turns APIC class queries into a typed, validated fabric inventory.
learning_objectives: Learners can authenticate to the APIC with aaaLogin and keep the session alive with aaaRefresh [c8].
Learners can write class queries with filters and subtree options for nodes, firmware and cluster state [c8][c11].
Learners can define a Pydantic inventory record and reject incomplete nodes with a clear reason.
Learners can test the client with pytest against recorded fixtures and review every Claude-written diff.

lessons.title: Session handling
points: POST {"aaaUser": {"attributes": {"name": ..., "pwd": ...}}} to /api/aaaLogin.json; the token arrives as APIC-cookie and in the response [c8].
Use the apic:domain\user form when the fabric has several login domains [c8].
Default session timeout is 600 seconds; call aaaRefresh before refreshTimeoutSeconds and store the new token each time [c8].
Wrap the session in a small class with retry on 401 and a hard timeout per request.

lessons.title: The queries behind the inventory
points: fabricNode for id, role, model, serial and fabricSt; topSystem for address, uptime and state.
firmwareCtrlrRunning for APIC versions and firmwareRunning for switch versions [c11].
infraWiNode for cluster membership and health as seen by each APIC.
Use query-target-filter (for example eq(fabricNode.role,"leaf")), rsp-subtree-include=health and page/page-size for large fabrics [c8].
vPC pairing comes from the vPC protection group configuration; record the peer id for every leaf so the planner can split pairs [c3].
Capture each query string in the record so later explanations can cite it.

lessons.title: Typed inventory and rejected rows
points: Inventory node fields: node_id, name, role, model, running_version, vpc_peer, health_score, apic_connected, pod, source_queries.
Cluster fields: apic_id, version, health, and a cluster_fully_fit flag computed in code, never by the model.
Pydantic validation turns a missing version or unknown role into a rejected row with a reason, not a silent default.
Write inventory.json and rejected.json; a non-empty rejected file fails the pipeline step.

lessons.title: Working with Claude Code on the client
points: Ask Claude Code to write the client in small steps: session, one query, model, then tests.
Read every diff; reject code that hard-codes credentials or disables TLS verification.
Generate pytest tests from recorded JSON fixtures, including a node without firmwareRunning data.
Use the DevNet simulator for extra API practice; it is shared or time-limited, so record fixtures for repeatable tests [c37].

instructor_demo: curl the aaaLogin endpoint and show the token and refreshTimeoutSeconds in the response [c8].
Run a fabricNode class query with a role filter, then the same with rsp-subtree-include=health [c8].
Ask Claude Code to implement ApicSession with refresh, and review the diff line by line.
Add the Pydantic model and show validation rejecting a fixture with a missing version.
Run pytest and show the coverage of happy path, missing data and expired token.
Produce inventory.json for the lab fabric and open it next to the GUI.

lab.brief: Implement the discovery client and tests with Claude Code, inspect every diff, and produce inventory.json for the lab fabric.
steps: Record fixtures from the lab APIC for fabricNode, topSystem, firmwareCtrlrRunning, firmwareRunning and infraWiNode [c11].
Have Claude Code write the session class with aaaLogin, aaaRefresh and retry; review and commit [c8].
Add query helpers with filters and paging [c8].
Define InventoryNode and ClusterState Pydantic models.
Join the queries into one inventory and compute cluster_fully_fit in code.
Write rejected rows with reasons to rejected.json.
Write pytest tests for each query, the join and two broken fixtures.
Run against the lab and save inventory.json and the query log.
success_criteria: inventory.json lists all 3 APICs, 4 leaves and 2 spines with versions and vPC peers.
A deliberately broken fixture produces a rejected row, not a crash or a default value.
Tests pass offline using fixtures only.
No credentials or disabled TLS checks in the committed code.

common_pitfalls: Treating an empty result as 'no faults' when the query itself failed.
Letting the token expire during long paging loops [c8].
Using node names instead of node ids as keys; ids are what maintenance groups reference [c10].
Accepting Claude-generated code without reading it, especially around TLS and secrets.

knowledge_check.q: What do you do before refreshTimeoutSeconds runs out?
knowledge_check.a: Call aaaRefresh and replace the stored token with the new one it returns [c8].

knowledge_check.q: Which options limit a class query to leaves and include health?
knowledge_check.a: query-target-filter=eq(fabricNode.role,"leaf") and rsp-subtree-include=health [c8].

knowledge_check.q: Why does the inventory store a vpc_peer field for every leaf?
knowledge_check.a: The planner must put vPC peers in different groups; Cisco requires one leaf of each pair to stay up [c3].

knowledge_check.q: A node has no running version in the response. What does the client do?
knowledge_check.a: It writes a rejected row with the reason and fails the step; it never guesses a version.

modules.title: Pre-upgrade validation and explained failures
modules.goal: Learners run Cisco's validators, parse their results into structured findings, and have Claude explain each failure with the query behind it and Cisco's remediation.
learning_objectives: Learners can run the standalone pre-upgrade validation script and locate its result bundle [c5][c6].
Learners can call the APIC pre-validation endpoints available from 5.1(1) and the built-in validator through an update group [c4][c10].
Learners can check faults, bootflash, cluster health, NTP, CIMC and backups against the checklist [c12][c21].
Learners can produce a validation report where Claude explains every FAIL in plain language and marks unknowns.

lessons.title: Cisco's validation options
points: Built-in Pre-Upgrade Validator runs when an update group is configured; the App Center app is obsolete (App Center deprecated in 6.1.2); the standalone script runs from the APIC CLI [c4].
Run the script at least two weeks before the window so fixes have time to land [c4].
From 6.2(1) external rules are pulled into the Upgrade GUI through Intersight or a manual rules package [c4].

REST pre-validation from 5.1(1): GET /mqapi2/deployment.query.json?mode=validateCtrlrMaintP&targetVersion=..., and mode=validateSwitchMaintP or the async form with getSwitchPreValStatus polling [c10].

lessons.title: Running and parsing the script
points: Copy aci-preupgrade-validation-script.py to /data/techsupport, run python aci-preupgrade-validation-script.py, give admin credentials and pick a target version that is already on the APIC [c5].
The sample run reports 47 checks, from NTP status and switch /bootflash usage to VPC-paired leaf switches [c6].
Results land in /data/techsupport/preupgrade_validator_<timestamp>.tgz with a debug log, a JSON results file and a text dump [c6].
Parse the JSON results file, not the console text, into Finding records: check, status, detail, recommended action.
Statuses the course handles explicitly: FAIL and MANUAL CHECK REQUIRED; anything not recognised becomes UNKNOWN [c5].

lessons.title: The checks that matter most
points: Faults: clear all faults before upgrading, except those expected from staging [c12].
Bootflash: F1820 at 80% and F1821 at 90%; the script compares free space with what the target needs, generally twice the image size [c12][c21].
Cluster and switches: every APIC Fully Fit (acidiag cluster), all switches Active, standby APIC filesystems under 75% [c12][c21].
NTP on APICs and switches with reachability; CIMC version per the release notes; an AES-encrypted config export [c12][c9].
MD5 of the image checked on the file server, the uploaded copy, each APIC repository and each switch bootflash [c12].

lessons.title: Claude explains, code decides
points: Code decides pass or fail; Claude only writes the explanation, the likely cause and Cisco's documented remediation.
Every explanation cites the finding id and the APIC query or script check that produced it.
If the evidence does not show a cause, Claude must write 'unknown' and list what to collect next.
Output is a ValidationReport schema through structured outputs so the explanation can be gated like the plan [c26].

instructor_demo: Copy the script to /data/techsupport on the lab APIC and run it against the course target release [c5].
Extract the .tgz and open the JSON results file [c6].

modules.title: Upgrade planning with structured outputs
modules.goal: Learners have Claude propose upgrade groups and windows as structured output, then prove that code rejects any plan that breaks Cisco's grouping rules.
learning_objectives: Learners can encode Cisco's group rules as code checks [c3].
Learners can generate an UpgradePlan as schema-validated structured output from inventory and validation results [c26].
Learners can map groups to maintenance windows in the fabric's local time zone.
Learners can test the planner against awkward fabrics and show it rejects bad plans.

lessons.title: Rules from Cisco, written as code
points: Order: APIC cluster first, switch groups only after the cluster is Fully Fit [c2].
At least two groups; vPC peers in different groups; one APIC-connected leaf per APIC up; at least one route-reflector spine and one IPN-connected spine per pod up [c3].
Separate redundant non-vPC leaves such as border leaves too [c20].
With graceful upgrade enforced, the APIC rejects upgrading the last spine in a pod; one-spine pods need graceful disabled [c3].
Run mode per group: pauseOnlyOnFailures is the APIC default and the course default [c10][c22].

lessons.title: The plan schema
points: UpgradePlan: plan_id, fabric, target_version, intermediate_version, apic_step, groups[], windows[], risks[], unknowns[], source_inventory_hash.
Group: name, node_ids, role_mix, run_mode, graceful, window_ref, rationale.
Window: start and end in ISO 8601 with offset (for example +05:30 for IST), change_ref.
Pass the Pydantic schema as output_format and read structured_output [c26].
Validation happens twice: JSON Schema shape in the SDK, then the rule checks in Python.

lessons.title: Windows and time zones
points: Every window carries an explicit offset; the runner compares times in UTC.
From 5.1 the GUI has no scheduler; the course runner decides when to trigger, inside the approved window [c17].
Allow time for pre-download before the install window; the 5.1+ workflow downloads first, then Begin Install [c16].
A multistep upgrade needs a window per hop [c2].

lessons.title: Testing the planner
points: Fixtures: the lab fabric, a fabric with an unpaired vPC leaf, mixed leaf models, a degraded APIC, a single-spine pod.
Expected outcome per fixture written first, then the planner run.
A degraded APIC means no plan, only a blocking finding [c12].
An unpaired leaf is flagged because vPC protection cannot work for it [c12].

instructor_demo: Show the rule checks in plan_rules.py next to the Cisco guideline text [c3].

Run the degraded APIC fixture and show the planner returns a blocking finding instead of a plan.
Show a window with a missing offset failing schema validation [c26].

lab.brief: Generate the plan for the lab fabric, feed it a fabric with an unpaired vPC leaf, and prove the schema gate rejects the bad plan.
steps: Write the UpgradePlan Pydantic models.
Implement rule checks for vPC split, APIC-connected leaves, spines per pod and order [c3].
Write the planner prompt with inventory.json and findings.json as inputs.
Run the planner with output_format and save plan.json [c26].
Run the gate on plan.json.
Run the planner on the unpaired-leaf fixture and record the gate result.
Run the degraded APIC and single-spine fixtures.
Commit plans, gate results and tests.
success_criteria: The lab plan passes and puts leaf-101/leaf-102 and leaf-103/leaf-104 in different groups with one spine each.
The unpaired-leaf fixture is flagged and a hand-edited bad plan is rejected with a named rule.
The degraded APIC fixture produces no plan.
All windows carry explicit offsets.

common_pitfalls: Letting Claude's rationale text count as validation.
Putting both spines of a two-spine pod in one group [c3].
Using local times without offsets.
Forgetting that run mode and graceful are per policy, so groups with different settings need different policies [c22].

knowledge_check.q: What happens if both members of a vPC pair are in the same group?
knowledge_check.a: Cisco's rule is broken; the course gate rejects the plan. Cisco notes that in that case only one is upgraded at a time, but the course never relies on that [c3].

knowledge_check.q: Why does a one-spine pod matter when graceful upgrade is enforced?
knowledge_check.a: The APIC rejects upgrading the last spine in a pod under graceful upgrade, so the plan must disable graceful for that pod or the group fails [c3].

knowledge_check.q: Where does the validated plan come from in the SDK?
knowledge_check.a: structured_output on a successful ResultMessage; error_max_structured_output_retries means no valid plan [c26].

knowledge_check.q: What does the planner return for a degraded APIC?
knowledge_check.a: A blocking finding and no plan, because the cluster must be Fully Fit before switch upgrades [c2].

modules.title: Firmware staging, backups and the change request
modules.goal: Learners stage the target image, take and verify a configuration snapshot, and raise a ServiceNow change from the approved plan with one command.
learning_objectives: Learners can register firmware sources and verify the image checksum at each point Cisco lists [c7][c12].
Learners can take a configuration snapshot through configExportP and wait for it to complete [c23].
Learners can create a normal change through the ServiceNow API with plan, windows and risk text [c31][c33].
Learners can read the change state and approval state and block execution until it is approved [c32][c34].

lessons.title: Firmware repository
points: Register the image with firmwareRepoP and firmwareOSource (name, proto, url) at /api/node/mo/uni/fabric.xml [c7].
Images for APICs and switches are downloaded to the APICs; switches pull firmware from the APICs later [c2].
Check MD5 on the file server, after upload, in each APIC's repository and on each switch's bootflash [c12].
If the image is missing on an APIC, wait about five minutes, then remove and re-download through the GUI or API, never with rm [c12].

lessons.title: Backups and snapshots
points: Cisco asks for a configuration export with AES encryption before the upgrade [c12].
Record the encryption passphrase; TAC notes passwords will not import correctly without the key [c20].
Snapshots are created through configExportP with snapshot enabled; max_count defaults to 3 and rolls over [c23].
Pause and poll until the snapshot exists before comparing or relying on it [c23].
Store the snapshot name and export location in the evidence bundle.

lessons.title: The ServiceNow change
points: Create a normal change through the Change Management API, or a change_request record through the Table API in a PDI [c31][c33].

Fields: short_description, description (plan summary), justification, implementation plan, backout plan, risk and impact text drafted by Claude, start_date and end_date from the plan windows, cmdb_ci.
Only one change is created per call; store the returned sys_id and number [c31][c33].
Roles: change_manager, itil or admin for POST and PATCH [c31].

lessons.title: Approval tracking
points: Normal change states: New, Assess, Authorize, Scheduled, Implement, Review, Closed [c32].
The runner treats Scheduled (-2) or Implement (-1) with approval approved as the only go states [c32].
A Flow Designer flow with Ask for Approval and a Due Date notifies the CAB and stops waiting forever [c34].
Poll with GET and sysparm_fields to keep payloads small [c33].

instructor_demo: Post firmwareRepoP for the switch and APIC images and watch the download in Admin > Firmware > Images [c7].
Compare MD5 values at each point and write them to evidence/md5.json [c12].
Run the snapshot playbook with a pause, then list snapshots [c23].
Run snow change create --plan plan.json against the PDI and show the record [c31].
Show the flow sending an approval request and the change moving from Assess to Authorize [c32][c34].

lab.brief: Stage the target image, take the snapshot, and raise the lab ServiceNow change from the plan with one command.
steps: Upload the target images to the lab file server and record MD5.
Register them on the APIC and wait for download [c7].
Verify MD5 on the APIC repositories and record results [c12].
Run the AES-encrypted export and the snapshot through the Ansible module with a pause [c23].
Ask Claude to draft the change text from plan.json and review it.
Run the change create command against the PDI [c31][c33].
Build or import the approval flow with a Due Date [c34].
Poll the change and confirm the runner reports 'blocked: not approved'.
success_criteria: Images present on all APICs with matching MD5.
A completed snapshot whose name is recorded in evidence.
One change record created from one command, with windows matching the plan.
The runner refuses to proceed while the change is not in an approved state.

common_pitfalls: Comparing snapshots before they finish [c23].
Losing the export passphrase [c20].
Creating duplicate change records on retry; check for an existing change by plan_id first.
Treating Assess as approved [c32].

knowledge_check.q: Which class creates a configuration snapshot?
knowledge_check.a: configExportP; configSnapshot is used to remove snapshots [c23].

knowledge_check.q: Name the four points where Cisco says to check image MD5.
knowledge_check.a: On the file server or desktop, the uploaded APIC copy, each APIC's firmware repository, and each switch's bootflash [c12].

knowledge_check.q: Which change states let the runner proceed?
knowledge_check.a: Only an approved change in Scheduled or Implement; New, Assess and Authorize block [c32].

knowledge_check.q: Why does the approval flow have a Due Date?
knowledge_check.a: So the flow does not wait forever for an approval [c34].

modules.title: Guardrails, approvals and audit for fabric upgrades
modules.goal: Learners build the gates that keep the agent read-only, require approved pull requests and changes, enforce windows and health, and record everything in an audit log.
learning_objectives: Learners can show that only deterministic Python or Ansible creates maintenance and firmware policies [c10][c22].
Learners can configure a pull request gate with required reviews and status checks [c36].
Learners can enforce windows and health so no group starts outside its window or after an unhealthy group [c11].
Learners can produce an audit log a change board can read.

lessons.title: The agent reads; code writes
points: No write tool on the MCP server; Bash, Write and Edit denied for the agent session [c28].
A PreToolUse hook denies any tool call whose name or arguments mention maintMaintP, adminSt or triggered [c27].
Policies are created by runner/apply.py or Ansible cisco.aci modules with admin_state untriggered [c22].
The trigger is a separate step that checks change state, window and health before posting adminSt=triggered [c10].

lessons.title: Pull request and change gates
points: plan.json lives in a branch; a PR to main requires one approval from netops-lead and dismisses stale approvals on new commits [c36].
Required status checks: schema validation, rule checks and a fresh validator result [c36].
Apply to admins too so nobody bypasses the gate [c36].
The apply job also checks the ServiceNow change state and refuses if not approved [c32].

lessons.title: Window and health enforcement
points: The runner refuses to trigger if now is outside the window from the approved change.
No next group until every node in the last group runs the target version and the cluster is Fully Fit [c11][c2].
If validation is incomplete or stale, the next step is blocked.
Do not change the switch firmware group mid-upgrade; Cisco says the upgrade will not complete [c15].

lessons.title: Audit log
points: Events: prompt, model output hash, tool call, APIC request and response code, approval, gate decision, operator.
Append-only JSON lines with a run id, signed off by hash chaining each line.
The MCP spec expects clients to log tool usage for audit [c29].
Render a change-board summary from the log: who approved, what ran, what was refused.

instructor_demo: Open PR #87 with plan.json and show checks running.
Run make apply before approval and show the refusal and the audit entry.
Show the hook blocking the agent from calling a fake trigger tool [c27].
Approve the PR and the change in the PDI, re-run apply, and show policies created with adminSt untriggered [c22].
Try to trigger outside the window and show the refusal.

lab.brief: Open the plan as a pull request, try to apply it before approval and watch the gate refuse, then approve and apply to the lab.
steps: Configure branch protection on main with one required review and required checks [c36].
Write the GitHub Actions workflow that runs schema, rules and validator freshness checks.
Add the change-state check to apply.py [c32].
Add the hook and deny rules for the agent session [c27][c28].
Open the plan PR and attempt apply before approval.
Approve PR and change; apply and confirm policies exist untriggered.
Attempt a trigger outside the window.
Export the audit log and the change-board summary.
success_criteria: Apply before approval is refused and logged.
After approval, maintenance policy and group exist with adminSt untriggered.
Trigger outside the window is refused.
The audit summary lists every gate decision with time and actor.

common_pitfalls: Admins bypassing branch protection because 'include administrators' is off [c36].
Creating the policy with admin_state triggered by mistake [c22].
Checking the window in local time without an offset.
Logging secrets in the audit file.

knowledge_check.q: Which attribute actually starts a switch group upgrade?
knowledge_check.a: adminSt="triggered" on the maintenance policy (maintMaintP) [c10].

knowledge_check.q: What does dismissing stale approvals protect against?
knowledge_check.a: A reviewer approving one plan and a different plan being merged after new commits [c36].

knowledge_check.q: Why is a PreToolUse hook used as well as missing tools?
knowledge_check.a: Hooks run first and can deny a call even in permissive modes, giving defence in depth [c27][c28].

knowledge_check.q: What must be true before the next group starts?
knowledge_check.a: All nodes in the last group report the target version, maintUpgJob shows completion, the cluster is Fully Fit and the window is still open [c11].

modules.title: Executing the APIC cluster and switch group upgrades
modules.goal: Learners run a deterministic runner that upgrades the APIC cluster, then each switch group inside its window, and pauses safely when a node does not return.
learning_objectives: Learners can drive the APIC cluster upgrade by REST and wait for Fully Fit [c7][c13].
Learners can create and trigger switch maintenance policies and groups per the plan [c10][c22].
Learners can poll firmwareRunning and maintUpgJob with timeouts and pause on failure [c11].
Learners can have Claude draft an on-call status update from runner state.

lessons.title: APIC cluster upgrade
points: Set firmwareCtrlrFwP version, then post maintCtrlrMaintP adminSt=triggered [c7].
APICs install in parallel but convert and reload one at a time; the API is unavailable on the APIC that is converting [c13].
Poll firmwareCtrlrRunning and the cluster health from a different APIC than the one reloading [c11].
Before 6.0(6) done means all APICs online and Fully-Fit; from 6.0(6) wait for Post Upgrade Pending to become Completed [c13].
Never reload an APIC during conversion; if stuck, follow Cisco's stop rules and TAC steps [c13][c15][c20].

lessons.title: Switch groups
points: From 4.0(1): maintMaintP with version and runMode, maintMaintGrp with fabricNodeBlk and maintRsMgrpp [c10].
Pre-download first; install only when all nodes are ready [c16].
Trigger with adminSt=triggered inside the window [c10].
Each switch checks bootflash, extracts, updates grub, may upgrade BIOS/EPLD and reloads, sometimes twice for SSD firmware [c14].

lessons.title: Polling, timeouts and pause
points: Poll maintUpgJob and firmwareRunning per node every 30 seconds with a per-node timeout from the plan [c11].
If a node misses its timeout, pause: do not trigger the next group, keep polling, alert on-call.
Run mode pauseOnlyOnFailures matches this behavior on the APIC side [c10][c22].
Retries are for reads only; triggers are never retried automatically.

lessons.title: Recorded failure paths
points: A mocked APIC replays recorded responses: node stuck at a status, node missing from firmwareRunning, 503 during conversion.
The runner is tested against each recording in pytest.
Claude drafts the status update from runner state: what ran, what is stuck, what was not done, next decision owner.
The draft is posted only after a person reads it; the runner never pages anyone with model text alone.

instructor_demo: Show runner state machine: cluster, wait fully fit, group A, verify, group B.
Run the cluster step on the lab and narrate the serial reloads [c13].
Trigger group A in the window and watch maintUpgJob [c11].
Replay the node-not-returning recording and show the pause and the drafted status update.
Show the audit lines written for each step.

lab.brief: Run the APIC cluster upgrade and group A on the physical lab fabric, then replay a recorded node-not-returning response from a mocked APIC and watch the runner pause.
steps: Confirm change approved, window open and fresh validation PASS.
Run the cluster step and wait for Fully Fit or Completed [c13].
Re-run validation after the APIC upgrade [c2].
Create group A policies untriggered, review, then trigger in window [c10].
Poll until group A completes and record per-node durations [c11].
Start the mock APIC with the node-not-returning recording.
Run the runner against the mock and confirm it pauses and does not trigger group B.
Save the drafted status update and audit log.
success_criteria: APIC cluster on target and Fully Fit before any switch moves.
Group A on target with no trigger outside the window.
Against the mock, the runner pauses and never triggers group B.
The status update states facts from runner state only.

common_pitfalls: Polling the APIC that is converting and treating its silence as failure [c13].
Retrying a trigger after a timeout.
Changing the firmware group mid-upgrade [c15].
Skipping the second validation run [c2].

knowledge_check.q: In what order do APICs convert and reload?
knowledge_check.a: One at a time; the next starts only after the previous one is back online [c13].

knowledge_check.q: Which three classes do you poll during switch upgrades?
knowledge_check.a: maintUpgJob for job status, firmwareRunning for switch versions and firmwareCtrlrRunning for controllers [c11].

knowledge_check.q: What does the runner do if a node misses its timeout?
knowledge_check.a: Pause, keep reading, alert on-call and wait for a person; it never starts the next group or re-triggers.

knowledge_check.q: What status means a 6.0(6)+ APIC upgrade is finished?
knowledge_check.a: Completed, after Post Upgrade Pending [c13].

modules.title: Post-upgrade verification, reporting and rollback decisions
modules.goal: Learners compare pre and post state in code, have Claude write the report and recommendation, and make a documented go, hold or roll back decision.
learning_objectives: Learners can capture pre and post snapshots of versions, faults, endpoints, routes, vPC and interfaces and diff them in code [c8][c11].
Learners can produce a readable report with a go, hold or roll back recommendation signed by a person.
Learners can explain Cisco's downgrade constraints and when to stop the next group [c12][c15].
Learners can update the runbook with lessons for the next fabric.

lessons.title: What to compare
points: Versions: firmwareRunning and firmwareCtrlrRunning against the target [c11].
Faults: faultInst counts by severity, ordered by severity [c8].
Endpoints, routes, vPC and interface state from class queries taken before group A and after each group.
The comparison is code: counts, sets and thresholds, written to diff.json.

lessons.title: Report and recommendation
points: Claude receives diff.json and writes the report with sections: what changed, what did not, concerns, recommendation.
Recommendation values are fixed: GO, HOLD, ROLLBACK; the schema rejects anything else [c26].
Any new critical fault or vPC down means HOLD by rule, whatever the text says.
A person signs the decision and the signature goes in the audit log.

lessons.title: Rollback and downgrade
points: Downgrade has its own checklist: features not supported on older releases must be removed first [c12].
Downgrading APICs from 6.2 or newer to before 6.2(1) is not supported [c15].
The old switch image sits in the recovery partition after upgrade [c14].
Config rollback from a snapshot is a separate, approved change [c23].
Stopping the next group is the usual first move; the guide has a chapter on which operations are allowed while switches run mixed versions, so read it before holding for long [c1].

lessons.title: Runbook capture
points: Record per-node durations, surprises and fixes.
Update CLAUDE.md rules if the planner needs a new constraint [c24].
Add new fixtures for failure modes seen.
Note which validator checks were MANUAL CHECK REQUIRED and how the team resolved them [c5].

instructor_demo: Run collect --phase pre and --phase post-A and show diff.json.
Generate the report and show the fixed recommendation field.
Introduce a synthetic new critical fault in the post fixture and show HOLD forced by rule.
Walk the downgrade checklist and the 6.2 limit [c12][c15].

lab.brief: Compare pre and post state for group A, generate the report, and make the go or hold call for group B as a team.
steps: Load pre-upgrade snapshot data.
Collect post-group-A data.
Run the diff and review it.
Generate the report through structured output [c26].
Discuss as a team and record GO or HOLD with signature.
If GO, schedule group B in the next window; if HOLD, write the hold note.
Add three runbook entries.
success_criteria: diff.json covers versions, faults, endpoints, routes, vPC and interfaces.
The report recommendation matches the rules.
The decision is signed and logged.
Runbook updated.

common_pitfalls: Comparing against a stale pre snapshot.
Letting report prose override a rule-based HOLD.
Planning a downgrade without the downgrade checklist [c12].
Expecting endpoint counts to match exactly during learning after reboot; define tolerances.

knowledge_check.q: Who decides go or hold?
knowledge_check.a: A person, using the code diff and Claude's report; rules can force HOLD.

knowledge_check.q: Can you downgrade APICs from 6.2 to 6.1?
knowledge_check.a: No; Cisco says downgrading from 6.2 or newer to a release older than 6.2(1) is not supported [c15].

knowledge_check.q: Where does the previous switch image go after upgrade?
knowledge_check.a: To the recovery partition while the primary grub partition is updated to the target [c14].

knowledge_check.q: What is the first safe move when group A looks wrong?
knowledge_check.a: Hold group B and investigate; rollback is a separate approved change.

citations.title: Cisco APIC Installation and ACI Upgrade and Downgrade Guide
citations.supports: Course foundation; The Cisco ACI upgrade process and where upgrades go wrong
citations.key_fact: The guide is organized into an ACI Firmware Upgrade Overview, an Upgrade/Downgrade Architecture chapter, Pre-Upgrade/Downgrade Checklists, mixed-version operation guidance, and per-interface procedures (GUI by release including 5.1 or later and 6.2 or later, REST API, CLI).

citations.title: Upgrade or downgrade Cisco ACI fabrics (workflow)
citations.supports: The Cisco ACI upgrade process; Executing the APIC cluster and switch group upgrades
citations.key_fact: Cisco's workflow: back up the configuration with AES encryption, disable App Center apps, download APIC and switch images to the APICs, run pre-upgrade validation, update CIMC/BIOS/HUU components, upgrade the APICs, validate again, wait until all APICs are Fully Fit, then upgrade the ACI-mode switches; a multistep upgrade repeats the cycle from the intermediate release.

citations.title: Guidelines for ACI switch upgrades and downgrades
citations.supports: Upgrade planning with structured outputs; The Cisco ACI upgrade process
citations.key_fact: Divide leaf and spine switches into at least two update groups (ODD/EVEN example) so one leaf of each vPC pair, one leaf connected to each APIC, and at least one route-reflector spine and one IPN-connected spine per pod stay up; from APIC 4.2(5) switches in a group upgrade simultaneously with unlimited default concurrency, so Cisco recommends separate groups for separate schedules. Graceful upgrade uses GIR before reboot, the APIC rejects upgrading the last spine in a pod when graceful upgrade is enforced (from 4.1(1)), and switches already in GIR maintenance mode are not supported for firmware upgrades.

citations.title: Pre-upgrade validation tools
citations.supports: Pre-upgrade validation and explained failures
citations.key_fact: Three validation options exist: the built-in Pre-Upgrade Validator that runs automatically when an update group is configured, the App Center app (obsolete, App Center deprecated in 6.1.2), and the standalone script run from the APIC CLI; Cisco advises running the script at least two weeks before the maintenance window, and from APIC 6.2(1) external rules are pulled into the Upgrade GUI via Intersight or a manually uploaded rules package.

citations.title: GitHub - datacenter/ACI-Pre-Upgrade-Validation-Script
citations.supports: Pre-upgrade validation and explained failures
citations.key_fact: Copy aci-preupgrade-validation-script.py to /data/techsupport on an APIC, run it with python, enter admin-level credentials and choose a target version that is already on the APIC; checks flagged FAIL or MANUAL CHECK REQUIRED come with recommended actions and the run ends with a count per status.

citations.title: Introduction - ACI Pre-Upgrade Validation Script documentation
citations.supports: Pre-upgrade validation and explained failures
citations.key_fact: The example run reports TOTAL: 47 checks, including NTP Status, Switch Node /bootflash usage and VPC-paired Leaf switches (shown as MANUAL CHECK REQUIRED), and saves output plus debug data to /data/techsupport/preupgrade_validator_<timestamp>.tgz, which contains a debug log, a JSON results file and a text dump.

citations.title: Upgrade or downgrade the Cisco APIC software using the REST API
citations.supports: Firmware staging, backups and the change request; Executing the APIC cluster and switch group upgrades
citations.key_fact: A controller upgrade via REST is three POSTs: register the image source with firmwareRepoP/firmwareOSource (name, proto, url) at /api/node/mo/uni/fabric.xml, set the target version with firmwareCtrlrFwP (version, ignoreCompat) at /api/node/mo/uni/controller.xml, then trigger with maintCtrlrMaintP adminState="up" adminSt="triggered" at the same controller URL.

citations.title: Cisco APIC REST API Configuration Guide, Release 4.2(x) and Later - Using the REST API
citations.supports: Fabric discovery through the APIC REST API
citations.key_fact: Clients POST an aaaUser name/pwd to /api/aaaLogin.json (prefixing apic:domain\ when several login domains exist), get a token in the APIC-cookie and the refreshTimeoutSeconds attribute (default session timeout 600 seconds), and call aaaRefresh before expiry, storing the new token each time. Class queries use /api/node/class/<class>.json and object queries /api/node/mo/<dn>.json, with options query-target (self, children, subtree), target-subtree-class, query-target-filter such as eq(...), rsp-subtree-include=faults,health, order-by and page/page-size (example order-by=faultInst.severity|desc&page=0&page-size=15).

citations.title: Cisco APIC Release Notes, Release 6.1(4)
citations.supports: The Cisco ACI upgrade process (release notes and compatibility)
citations.key_fact: Release 6.1(4h) became available on August 13, 2025; the notes say to install only the CIMC versions in the compatibility table (other firmware can stop an APIC booting) and point to software advisory CSCwo74485 before upgrading listed UCS C225 M6 (APIC-L4/M4) CIMC versions.

citations.title: Upgrade or downgrade switch software using the REST API
citations.supports: Executing the APIC cluster and switch group upgrades; Guardrails, approvals and audit for fabric upgrades
citations.key_fact: Switch upgrades via REST: add the image with firmwareRepoP/firmwareOSource at /api/node/mo/uni/fabric.xml; from 4.0(1) create a maintMaintP with version and runMode="pauseOnlyOnFailures" and a maintMaintGrp containing fabricNodeBlk (from_/to_) entries and a maintRsMgrpp relation to the policy; trigger by posting maintMaintP with adminSt="triggered". From 5.1(1) the guide adds pre-validation calls such as /mqapi2/deployment.query.json?mode=validateCtrlrMaintP&targetVersion=... and mode=validateSwitchMaintP / validateSwitchMaintPAsync with getSwitchPreValStatus polling.

citations.title: Verify the firmware version and the upgrade status using the API
citations.supports: Executing the APIC cluster and switch group upgrades; Fabric discovery through the APIC REST API
citations.key_fact: Cisco documents three GETs: /api/node/class/firmwareCtrlrRunning.xml for controller firmware, /api/node/class/firmwareRunning.xml for switch firmware, and /api/node/class/maintUpgJob.xml for upgrade status of controllers and switches.

citations.title: Pre-Upgrade/Downgrade Checklists
citations.supports: Pre-upgrade validation and explained failures; Post-upgrade verification, reporting and rollback decisions
citations.key_fact: Checklist items include clearing all faults, a configuration export with AES encryption, OOB, CIMC and console access, every APIC Fully Fit (acidiag cluster on 4.2(1)+), all switches Active, standby APIC filesystems below 75%, NTP on APICs and switches, all switch nodes in vPC pairs, APIC disk faults F1527/F1528/F1529 and switch /bootflash faults F1820 (80%) and F1821 (90%), MD5 checks at four points, and a downgrade checklist of features unsupported on older releases.

citations.title: High level summary of APIC upgrades and downgrades
citations.supports: Executing the APIC cluster and switch group upgrades
citations.key_fact: Image installation runs on all APICs in parallel, but database conversion and reload happen one APIC at a time, the next starting only after the previous is back; during conversion DME processes and nginx are down on that APIC, so no disruptive action may be taken; before 6.0(6) the upgrade is complete when all APICs are online and Fully-Fit, and from 6.0(6) the status shows Post Upgrade Pending before Completed.

citations.title: How ACI switch upgrades and downgrades work
citations.supports: The Cisco ACI upgrade process; Executing the APIC cluster and switch group upgrades
citations.key_fact: The APIC pushes the image, the switch checks filesystem and bootflash space for extraction, extracts the image and updates the primary grub partition (the old version moves to the recovery partition), upgrades BIOS/EPLD if needed, does a clean reload and rejoins the fabric; from 2.1(4) an SSD firmware update can cause a second reboot.

citations.title: Guidelines and limitations for upgrading or downgrading
citations.supports: Post-upgrade verification, reporting and rollback decisions; Guardrails, approvals and audit for fabric upgrades
citations.key_fact: If an upgrade stalls or fails, do not reload any APIC, do not decommission a controller and do not switch the firmware target back to the original version; changing the switch firmware group during the upgrade stops the upgrade completing; downgrading APICs from 6.2 or newer to a release older than 6.2(1) is not supported; logs are not accessible while an APIC reboots.

citations.title: Leaf and spine switch upgrades and downgrades through APIC running release 5.1x or later
citations.supports: The Cisco ACI upgrade process; Upgrade planning with structured outputs
citations.key_fact: In Admin > Firmware > Switches an update group is created, nodes and image selected, Advanced Settings reviewed (Compatibility Check enforced by default, Graceful Upgrade unenforced by default, Run Mode Pause Upon Upgrade Failure / Pause Upon Install Failure / Never Pause), Update starts the pre-download, and Begin Install runs once all nodes show Ready to Install; Done is clicked when all nodes show Completed before moving to the next group.

citations.title: Upgrade or downgrade with APIC release 5.1 or later using the GUI
citations.supports: Upgrade planning with structured outputs; Guardrails, approvals and audit for fabric upgrades
citations.key_fact: Starting from release 5.1 the APIC GUI does not provide an option to set a scheduler for the upgrade; pre-download and related benefits are built into the native workflow instead.

citations.supports: Promo video research; The Cisco ACI upgrade process
citations.key_fact: Release 6.0(8e) became available on October 28, 2024, followed by 6.0(8f) on December 4, 2024 and 6.0(8h) on June 16, 2025; the companion switch software is Cisco Nexus 9000 ACI-Mode release 16.0(8).

citations.title: Cisco APIC Upgrade/Downgrade Support Matrix
citations.supports: The Cisco ACI upgrade process
citations.key_fact: The matrix takes direction (upgrade or downgrade), a from release and a to release, and returns changes in behavior and open and current-release bugs for APIC and switches; the listed paths have been tested and validated by Cisco, Cisco partners or both.

citations.title: ACI Upgrade Best Practices and Troubleshooting (TAC document 213618)
citations.supports: The Cisco ACI upgrade process; Executing the APIC cluster and switch group upgrades
citations.key_fact: Put vPC pair leaves and redundant non-vPC leaves such as border leaves in different maintenance groups; keep CIMC at the recommended version and use CIMC KVM if an APIC does not return; check acidiag avread (255 is healthy) before starting; never reboot two or more APICs at the same time; if APIC1 has not finished, do nothing on APIC2 and APIC3; a known failure is APIC2 stuck at 75%.

citations.title: Validations - ACI Pre-Upgrade Validation Script documentation
citations.supports: Pre-upgrade validation and explained failures
citations.key_fact: The /bootflash check compares each switch's available space with what the target release needs (generally twice the target image size) rather than a fixed percentage and reports available versus required space; F1820/F1821 thresholds are 80% and 90%; the standby APIC check runs df -h as rescue-user and alerts at 75%; the NTP check confirms all APICs and switches are synchronized.

citations.title: cisco.aci aci_maintenance_policy module source
citations.supports: Guardrails, approvals and audit for fabric upgrades; Executing the APIC cluster and switch group upgrades
citations.key_fact: The module manages maintMaintP at fabric/maintpol-{name} with options name, run_mode (pauseOnlyOnFailures default, pauseNever, pause_always_between_sets), graceful (default false), scheduler (required for state present, attached through maintRsPolScheduler), ignore_compat, admin_state triggered/untriggered (default untriggered; triggered starts an immediate upgrade), download_state and version.

citations.title: cisco.aci aci_config_snapshot module source
citations.supports: Firmware staging, backups and the change request
citations.key_fact: New snapshots are created with the configExportP class and removed with configSnapshot; options include export_policy, max_count (1-10, APIC default 3), include_secure (default true) and format (JSON default); the docs strongly recommend a pause after creating a snapshot and waiting until it finishes before querying, comparing or rolling back.

citations.title: How Claude remembers your project (CLAUDE.md)
citations.supports: Claude Code, Agent SDK and MCP setup for the ACI workflow
citations.key_fact: A project CLAUDE.md lives at ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md, /init generates a starting file, @path imports pull in other files (up to four hops), files should stay under about 200 lines, and CLAUDE.md is context rather than enforced configuration, so a PreToolUse hook is the way to block an action regardless of what Claude decides.

citations.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
citations.supports: Claude Code, Agent SDK and MCP setup for the ACI workflow
citations.key_fact: Stdio servers are added with claude mcp add [options] <name> -- <command> [args], with --env KEY=value and --scope local|project|user; project scope writes .mcp.json at the repository root for version control, project servers need approval before first use, /mcp shows status and tool counts, and .mcp.json supports ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} expansion.

citations.title: Get structured output from agents
citations.supports: Upgrade planning with structured outputs; Claude Code, Agent SDK and MCP setup for the ACI workflow
citations.key_fact: Pass output_format={"type": "json_schema", "schema": ...} to query(); a Pydantic model's model_json_schema() can supply the schema; the validated result arrives as structured_output on the ResultMessage, the SDK validates against JSON Schema draft-07 and re-prompts on mismatch, and a run that cannot produce valid output ends with subtype error_max_structured_output_retries.

citations.title: Hooks reference
citations.supports: Guardrails, approvals and audit for fabric upgrades
citations.key_fact: PreToolUse hooks run before a tool call and can block it with exit code 2 or JSON permissionDecision "deny"; MCP tools are named mcp__<server>__<tool> and matched with patterns such as mcp__memory__.*; hooks live in ~/.claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.json (committed) or .claude/settings.local.json.

citations.title: Configure permissions (Agent SDK)
citations.supports: Claude Code, Agent SDK and MCP setup for the ACI workflow; Guardrails, approvals and audit for fabric upgrades
citations.key_fact: The SDK checks hooks, then deny rules, ask rules, permission mode, allow rules and finally the canUseTool callback; disallowed_tools=["Bash"] removes a tool entirely and deny rules apply even in bypassPermissions; allowed_tools does not constrain bypassPermissions; pairing allowed_tools with permission_mode "dontAsk" gives a locked-down headless agent.

citations.title: Model Context Protocol specification: Tools
citations.supports: Claude Code, Agent SDK and MCP setup for the ACI workflow
citations.key_fact: Clients discover tools with tools/list and invoke them with tools/call; a tool has name, description, inputSchema, optional outputSchema and annotations (which clients must treat as untrusted unless the server is trusted); results can carry structuredContent and isError; there SHOULD always be a human in the loop able to deny invocations, servers MUST validate inputs and rate limit, and clients SHOULD log tool usage for audit.

citations.title: MCP Python SDK
citations.supports: Claude Code, Agent SDK and MCP setup for the ACI workflow
citations.key_fact: Install with uv add "mcp[cli]" or pip install "mcp[cli]" (Python 3.11+); tools are registered with the @mcp.tool() decorator and their schema comes from type hints and docstrings; stdio, Streamable HTTP and SSE transports are supported; uv run mcp dev server.py opens the server in the MCP Inspector.

citations.title: Change Management API
citations.supports: Firmware staging, backups and the change request
citations.key_fact: The API creates emergency or normal change requests and standard changes from published templates, processes related approvals, and offers GET /sn_chg_rest/change with sysparm_query, sysparm_offset and order; POST and PATCH need change_manager, itil or admin; one change request is created per call.

citations.title: Change Management state model
citations.supports: Firmware staging, backups and the change request; Guardrails, approvals and audit for fabric upgrades
citations.key_fact: Normal changes move New (-5), Assess (-4, peer and technical approval), Authorize (-3, Change Management and CAB approval), Scheduled (-2, approved and waiting for planned start), Implement (-1), Review (0) and Closed (3); Canceled is 4.

citations.title: Table API
citations.supports: Firmware staging, backups and the change request
citations.key_fact: The Table API lives at /api/now/table/{tableName}; POST inserts one record and returns 201 with a Location header; GET supports sysparm_query encoded queries (^ for AND, ^OR, ORDERBY/ORDERBYDESC), sysparm_fields, sysparm_limit and sysparm_display_value; PATCH /now/table/{tableName}/{sys_id} updates named fields.

citations.title: Ask for Approval action (Workflow Studio / Flow Designer)
citations.supports: Firmware staging, backups and the change request
citations.key_fact: The Ask for Approval core action takes a Record, a Table with an approval field, Approval Reason, Approval Field, Journal Field, approval Rules and a Due Date that stops a flow waiting forever; its Approval State output is Not Yet Requested, Requested, Approved, Rejected, Cancelled, No Longer Required or Skipped; flow_designer or admin role is needed.

citations.title: Get a development instance (ServiceNow PDI)
citations.supports: Lab environment
citations.key_fact: A free ServiceNow personal developer instance is obtained by signing in to the ServiceNow Developer Site and following the Personal Developer Instance (PDI) guide under Guides.

citations.title: About protected branches
citations.supports: Guardrails, approvals and audit for fabric upgrades
citations.key_fact: Protected branches can require a set number of approving reviews, required status checks that must be successful, skipped or neutral (strict mode also requires the branch to be up to date), code owner review, dismissal of stale approvals when new commits change the diff, and can apply the rules to administrators too.

citations.key_fact: DevNet offers a shared ACI Simulator (Always-On) with no reservation for APIC API requests, a reservable ACI Simulator sandbox for up to 5 consecutive days, and a Nexus Dashboard Orchestrator sandbox; the sandboxes are zero-cost.
